text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and create human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text. This training data includes books, websites, and articles, which helps the model learn grammar, facts, and ideas. To get good results, people use prompt engineering: writing clear instructions so the model gives useful answers. LLMs can help with writing, translating, and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes, cannot truly think, and may repeat false information from their training data.
